fixes.row: Blood-guilt: “his blood will be on his own head”, “no bloodguilt”, “bloodshed pollutes the land”
fixes.why: Matt 27:25 (“His blood be on us and on our children!”) is listed in this row with no caution beside it. The passion row carries the note that the verse has been read against the Jewish people, but this row has only a pointer, so a reader who meets the verse here gets the sentence without its context. The row's own note treats it as the same idiom as Acts 18:6, which is a different case.
fixes.fix: Remove Matt.27.25 from this row's verses (it stays in 'In the passion', where its note stands). Keep Matt.27.24 and Acts.5.28, which carry the phrase with Pilate's and the council's words. Alternatively keep it here with the passion row's caution repeated beside the verse.

fixes.row: The cup: “This is My blood”, “drink My blood”, “a participation in the blood of Christ”
fixes.why: The label puts John 6:53-56 under the Lord's cup. Placing the saying at Capernaum in the Supper row settles, by row order, the question the note says readers part on (whether John 6 speaks of the Supper). That breaks rule 2 and is most visible to readers who do not take John 6 as the Supper. The Lutheran, Catholic and Orthodox seats would not object to the verses, but the fairness test applies to the placement.
fixes.fix: Move John.6.53, 6.54, 6.55 and 6.56 into a new row labelled from the words, for example “Eating the flesh and drinking the blood: the saying at Capernaum (John 6)”, with the note saying readers part on whether it speaks of the Supper and the page takes no side. Retitle the cup row to “The cup: ‘This is My blood’, ‘the cup of blessing’, ‘a participation in the blood of Christ’”, dropping ‘drink My blood’. That makes 25 rows, the top of the brief's range.

fixes.row: “The life is in the blood”: not to be eaten or drunk
fixes.why: The label states a rule of not eating or drinking blood, and the Council's ‘from blood’ sits under it. The note itself says readers part on whether that letter binds, and on whether the blood there is eaten blood or bloodshed. The heading therefore reads the Council's words as the Leviticus rule before the reader has seen the dispute. That is a label saying more than the verses say (rule 1 and rule 2).
fixes.fix: Relabel to “‘The life is in the blood’: not to be eaten or drunk, and the Council's ‘from blood’ (Acts 15)”, so the Acts verses are named as a separate matter and the heading claims no more than the Leviticus verses do. Leave the note's paragraph on the dispute as it is.

fixes.row: Blood avenged and required: the avenger of blood; “How long ... until You ... avenge our blood?”
fixes.why: Psalm 72:14 says the king will redeem the poor from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight. The verse does not speak of avenging. It is in this row, under a heading about vengeance, and also in the redeemed row, where the note already quotes it. Placing it here reads the king's protection of the poor as vengeance, which is the justice framing a reader guarding against misreading would object to.
fixes.fix: Remove Ps.72.14 from this row's verses and from its note's sentence on the king (keep it in the redeemed row, where its note already sits).

fixes.row: Redeemed, purchased, released: “by Your blood You purchased for God”
fixes.why: The builder notes say Ps 72:14 has the Hebrew פָּדָה ‘redeem’ and that the Hebrew גָּאַל ‘redeem’ is not in any row with דָּם. The Berean's interlinear for Ps 72:14 shows יִגְאַל, from the root גָּאַל. So the note is wrong about the word, and the root is the one the avenged row's note says the avenger (גֹּאֵל) shares. The page does not equate the two, but the claim that the root is absent from these rows is false.
fixes.fix: Correct the builder _why for this row to say Ps 72:14 reads יִגְאַל (from גָּאַל, the root of the avenger's word גֹּאֵל in Num 35), and that the page does not make the two words one. Check the avenged row's _why for the same error after fix 5.

fixes.row: Blood in the rites of sacrifice: at the altar, sprinkled, poured out at its base
fixes.why: Rule 6 asks each example to show its label. Exod 23:18 (“You must not offer the blood of My sacrifices with anything leavened”) is one of the four examples a reader sees first, and it shows no altar, sprinkling or pouring out. The label is not visible in that example.
fixes.fix: In the example set, replace Exod.23.18 with Lev.4.18 (in this row's verses), which shows the blood on the altar and poured out at its base. Keep Exod.23.18 in the row's full verse list.

fixes.why: Two verses in the ‘others’ section show the English ‘flesh and blood’ for the Hebrew עֶצֶם ‘bone’ (2 Sam 5:1, the tribes' kinship with David) and מֵעִים ‘inward parts’ (2 Sam 16:11, David's own son). Neither entry has a note, unlike Isa 5:7 and Matt 9:20, so a reader is not told that these are not the blood word. Rule 4 is met in the rows (neither is placed there), but the section does not say so.
fixes.fix: Add a note to each entry: עֶצֶם ‘bone’ is the Hebrew for kin in 2 Sam 5:1, and מֵעִים is the Hebrew in 2 Sam 16:11; the Berean prints ‘flesh and blood’ for both, and the page does not make them the word דָּם.

worker_points.point: 1. What the blood does (rows 15 to 18, alphabetical, no ranking)
worker_points.why: The rows state the text's own phrases and the notes say readers part; the alphabetical order is announced and does not rank them.
The note gives the Greek ambiguity and says readers part on the meaning and on God; the page takes no side, and the verse sits in both rows without a settled reading.

worker_points.point: 3. The cup and the covenant (rows 19 and 20)
worker_points.why: John 6:53-56 placed under the cup heading settles by row order what the note says readers part on. See fix 2.

worker_points.point: 4. The life is in the blood / the eating of blood (row 2)
worker_points.why: The heading states the Council's ‘from blood’ as the same rule as Leviticus before the dispute is named. See fix 3.

The verse appears in the blood-guilt row with only a pointer; the sensitive note is in the passion row only. The rabbi's and the young African American believer's seats both need the caution beside the verse wherever it stands. See fix 1.
Row 21 names Christ, Jesus, the Son or the Lamb in each verse; row 22 holds the pronoun verses and its note names the passage that names him, which is the rule's form.
The note asks whose blood is on the robe and takes no side; the verse is a hard one and stays.
The note says readers take ‘a better word’ differently and takes no side; the verse is in both rows, each for a different point.
The note sets the avenger and the LORD's avenging beside the New Testament's word and takes no side, which is right. But Ps 72:14 is listed here, and it is not a vengeance verse. See fix 4.
The notes set the Passover and the Day of Atonement beside Hebrews 9 to 13 and point to the sacrifice page without choosing.
The note says only that the verse names an idol and the LORD's displeasure with those who choose their own ways, which is what the verse says.

examples_checked: 22 of 24 rows' examples show their label (the rites row's Exod.23.18 and the life row's Acts.15.20 do not; see fixes 5 and 3). The other examples were read in the Berean text in the built hub, and Matt 27:25 and Ps 72:14 were read through the local server.
summary: The hub holds up to a fair reading of the text: most rows state what their verses say and the contested points are set side by side with a note that takes no side. Seven fixes are needed before it ships: remove Matt 27:25 from the blood-guilt row, move John 6 out from under the cup, relabel the Acts 15 abstention, drop Ps 72:14 from the vengeance row, correct the builder note on Ps 72:14's Hebrew, replace one example in the rites row, and add notes to two 'others' entries.
